body:
> **Status:** Proposal; target LayerFS v0.1.7; not a released contract.

Release: [#155](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/155).
Implementation parent: [#165](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/165).
Core review: [#172](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/172) (Stage 7) reviews C1/C2 architecture flexibility and pluggability before subsequent integration design.
Sibling pairs: [#179](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/179) (projection & runtime) · [#180](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/180) (commit & history).

## Sequencing — owner direction, 2026-09-20

Stage 7 is a review of cluster 1 (content) + cluster 2 (storage), replacing its former runtime implementation scope. This co-design pair and its siblings own the subsequent integration design; implementation and integrated qualification are scoped after those designs. #171 remains the closed core qualification, not acceptance of a future runtime.

The integration must consume reviewed public contracts so that compatible C1/C2 algorithm revisions can be developed independently and substituted without rewriting integration logic. Record any required contract change explicitly; do not make integration depend on private content/storage algorithms, SQL or pack layouts. #172's parallel-worktree substitution scenario is the review's proof obligation, not an instruction to implement this pair during that review.

## Why this is a co-design pair

Three questions that each change the other two's answers:

```text
   ② LINK  ◄──── co-designed ────►  AUTHORIZATION  ◄────►  TENANCY
   ───────                          ─────────────            ───────
   what the frame carries           who may read root R      how many trust
   (does it carry a token?)         who may write objects    domains share
                                                             one owner
                  │                          │                      │
                  └──────────► what the OWNER MUST STORE ◄─────────┘
```

The authorization choice determines **both** what the frame carries (a capability
token?) **and** what the owner must hold (a `root → principal` map). And the tenant
count decides whether the owner needs that state at all.

**The tension to resolve:** a workspace-agnostic owner — the property that makes
N consumers × M workspaces cheap ([#179](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/179)) —
**cannot authorize per workspace.** It serves "read root R" and "store these
objects" and has no idea which workspace a root belongs to. Per-workspace
authorization forces the owner to hold state it currently does not.

## What it produces

- the frame format and the bounded-operation protocol
- the authorization mechanism, and whether the owner stays workspace-agnostic
- the tenant model and the storage topology it implies
- the deployment matrix realized as pluggable pieces rather than branches in code

## Already settled by discussion

| Decision | Why |
| --- | --- |
| **The owner is a role; a daemon is one realization** | embedded · standalone · remote are three deployments of one owner, not three designs |
| **All three via one pluggable link** | embedding is the degenerate case where the link is a function call |
| **Storage placement is owner-internal** | a consumer can never tell which cell it is in — that invisibility is what keeps the matrix small |
| **Six deployment cells reduce to two links** | direct ∣ byte stream (unix socket or TCP+TLS); the address differs, the code does not |
| **The link carries logical operations, not objects** | splitting at the C1/C2 traits would make one message per canonical object, which is the coupling the core architecture review must guard against |
| **Status codes mirror C1's error taxonomy** | `MissingObject` and `ProviderFailure` must stay distinguishable across the wire for the same reason they are distinct in-process |
| **Content-addressing gives the link its integrity** | a received object is verified by re-deriving its id, or transitively by the reuse byte-compare — no transport-level MAC is needed |

## Open

- [ ] **Frame format.** Length-prefixed bounded frames; what the header carries
      beyond the operation kind and the root; whether framing is shared with the
      object-batch path or separate.
- [ ] **Authorization mechanism.** Per-connection (all-or-nothing, zero owner
      state) · `root → principal` map (owner state, O(roots)) · capability tokens
      (stateless owner, needs a signer and key lifecycle). **This is the decision
      that forces the owner to stop being workspace-agnostic.**
- [ ] **Tenancy.** Single store with many projects (cross-project dedup — the
      product's value — one writer, one policy) versus store-per-tenant
      (isolation, no dedup). Note that single-tenant is the **simpler** option, not
      the more complex one; multi-tenant adds routing.
- [ ] **The cutoff constraint.** `small_file_threshold_bytes` is **per-store policy
      and changes canonical roots**, and `Store::open` has no migration path. Two
      projects wanting different cutoffs **cannot share a store** for the same
      content. If multi-tenancy is ever needed for policy reasons rather than
      isolation, this is why.
- [ ] **Backpressure and reconnection.** A dropped connection mid-save: the rule is
      "unknown acknowledgement is failure, no resend". A fresh flush of the same
      overlay is safe because content-addressing makes it idempotent — but whether
      that counts as a resend needs a ruling, not an assumption.
- [ ] **Whether the owner may be embedded at all in the shipped product**, or
      whether a daemon is mandatory once FUSE exists.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The operation set the link carries is enumerated, and its shape (bounded,
      batch, logical) is stated as a property rather than a convention.
- [ ] The frame format is specified with its bounds and its status taxonomy.
- [ ] Authorization is decided, and the consequence for the owner's state is
      stated explicitly — including whether the workspace-agnostic property is
      given up and what that costs.
- [ ] The tenant model is decided directionally **before** [#180](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/180)
      freezes a schema, because per-tenant policy would change it.
- [ ] The deployment matrix is expressed as composable pieces with the cell count
      stated, so the piece count does not grow with the cell count.
- [ ] Unsaved/unacknowledged state on connection loss is defined, with the
      no-durability posture preserved.
- [ ] No worker count, timeout or retry is added to make a case pass.

## Boundary

- **No cloud provider promise.** Cloudflare Durable Objects and D1 use WAL and are
  outside the current policy; radish is architectural inspiration, not a template.
  No provider registry, distributed lease service or speculative cloud package.
- **No durability change.** MEMORY journal, `synchronous = OFF`, no `fsync`, no
  WAL. A transport must not imply otherwise.
- **No new protocol without a concrete need.** The operations already exist and are
  bounded; mapping them onto frames is the job.
- **C1 and C2 import nothing from this pair.** No mount handles, daemon ids,
  transport types or tenancy concepts cross into the product core.

## Non-goals

- The projection and accumulator — [#179](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/179).
- Commit, stage and history semantics — [#180](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/180).
- Measured integration acceptance — define it with the subsequent implementation; #171 remains evidence for its core-only scope.
title: v0.1.7 co-design pair 3: boundary and trust — transport, authorization and tenancy
